transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-17 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Olivia Chen (Redwood AE); Marcus Patel (Redwood SE); Samira Gomez (Redwood CSM); James Holloway (Riverstone Head of Eng); Priya Nair (CTO); Evan Brooks (DevOps); Maya Lin (Product)

Summary (auto): Kickoff - high level goals: reduce inference latency for triage workflows to <200ms p95, integrate embeddings-based search into clinician UI, and ensure PHI controls for data in transit and at rest.

00:00 Olivia (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Olivia, AE on this account, and with me is Marcus, our SE, and Samira, your CSM. Quick roll call and then we'll go through goals.
00:12 James (Riverstone): Hey Olivia, James here. Priya here too. Evan and Maya on my side as well. Thanks, excited to get started.
00:20 Olivia: Awesome. High level, we want to align on success criteria, timeline, and security gating. Marcus will run through architecture options after the goals.
00:34 Priya (Riverstone): For context, our primary use case is a clinician-facing note summarization and search with embeddings. We have latency concerns — clinicians don't want wait — and of course PHI handling is critical.
00:48 Marcus (Redwood SE): Got it. Quick question on throughput — what's your expected QPS during peak?
00:55 James: For phase one, roughly 6 to 8 qps for the summarization route, embeddings indexing is batch but realtime search is around 20 qps at busy times.
01:10 Marcus: Cool, that maps well to a small dedicated pool. We can do hosted for initial eval but dedicated gives predictable throughput. We'll talk tradeoffs.
01:26 Samira (CSM): Onboarding timeline — what date are you targeting for pilot?
01:32 Priya: We'd like a pilot in early April, maybe 2–3 weeks, to validate latency and embeddings quality with a subset of clinicians.
01:42 Olivia: Early April is doable. We'll target a 2-week dedicated trial starting first week of April. We'll need your infra contacts for VPC peering if you want Private or Dedicated in your VPC.
01:55 Evan (DevOps): We are leaning toward Dedicated in our VPC via Private deployment. Main constraints: strict egress rules, KMS for keys, and we need audit logs forwarded to Splunk.
02:10 Marcus: All standard. We support customer-managed KMS (HSM integrations) and can stream audit logs. Small note: there are some kernel/quantization tradeoffs that affect CPU usage vs latency; we'll surface recommended quantization profiles.
02:28 James: Good. Security gating — SOC2 is a must for us and our legal folks want to review data retention and deletion policies.
02:37 Samira: We'll share the SOC2 pack and our standard retention controls doc after this call, along with our security contact.
02:46 Maya (Product): One product ask — can we run A/B tests with rollouts? We want canary style so clinicians don't get poor results.
02:54 Marcus: Yes, rollouts and canary traffic splitting are built-in. You can pin model versions; we also support automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant on errors.
03:07 Priya: Timeline question — after the pilot, what's the expected handoff and SLA?
03:13 Olivia: After a successful pilot we'll propose a Dedicated commit with an enterprise contract and support SLAs. Our CSM will run adoption and runbooks.
03:23 (short pause, crosstalk)
03:34 Marcus: Ok, I'm gonna share a high-level architecture screen — describing three options: Hosted (fastest onboarding), Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity in our infra, isolated), and Private (customer VPC / on-prem).
03:50 Marcus: Option one: Hosted API — minimal infra work, but data will traverse our network. Good for proofs but not ideal for strict PHI regs.
04:05 Marcus: Option two: Dedicated — we dedicate GPU pools and can enable VPC peering to limit exposure; predictable throughput and lower p95 latency.
04:18 Marcus: Option three: Private — full control, on-prem or VPC private deployment, required for some regulated flows, but longer lead time and ops coordination.
04:33 James: Sounds right. For us, private or dedicated in our VPC is preferable because of compliance.
04:42 Marcus: Understood. For the private/dedicated route we'll need network ranges, peering windows, and a list of required endpoints to open. Also KMS ARN for key management.
04:55 Evan: We'll compile that. Quick question — what regions do you support? We prefer east-1 and a eu option for redundancy.
05:03 Marcus: We have east-1, eu-west-1, and limited apac regions. For a pilot, east-1 is simplest.
05:12 Priya: Internal stakeholders — legal and security will need the SOC2 and encryption details. Can you provide an itemized checklist we can hand them?
05:20 Samira: Yes — I'll send the security checklist, and Olivia will include the onboarding guide.
05:28 Olivia: I'll also include an architecture template and a troubleshooting runbook.
05:35 (brief typing / shared link mention)
05:46 James: Another practical — token costs. We need visibility into per-route cost and a way to limit spend.
05:53 Marcus: Our console exposes token-level cost and per-route breakdowns; you can set quotas and alerts. We'll show that in the demo.
06:02 Maya: Can we also restrict models to specific teams to avoid accidental usage?
06:06 Samira: Yep, RBAC and route-level controls available. We'll include docs on SSO/SAML setup too.
06:13 Priya: Any known limitations with long-context note summarization (8k+ tokens)?
06:19 Marcus: Long contexts increase memory and some kernels don't scale linearly. We recommend chunking + KV cache and we'll suggest optimized kernels and quantization profiles. For very long docs private deployment with larger GPU footprints helps.
06:36 James: Ok that matches our intuition. For embeddings, what vector size do you recommend?
06:41 Marcus: Typically 1536 or 1024 depending on the model; we'll recommend based on your quality targets.
06:49 (short chuckle)
07:00 Olivia: Let's capture explicit success criteria — Priya, James, do these look right? 1) p95 latency for summarization under 200ms in clinician UI, 2) embeddings-based search recall > 0.85 on internal eval set, 3) SOC2 review complete, 4) pilot by early April.
07:20 Priya: Yes that's accurate. Add 5) seamless RBAC + SSO for clinician access.
07:27 Olivia: Great, we'll bake that into the pilot acceptance criteria.
07:33 (few seconds background)
07:40 Marcus: I'll call out a couple of tradeoffs — quantization lowers memory & cost but can slightly affect output quality; auto-batching can improve throughput but may add a small latency tail. We'll provide tuned configs.
07:56 Evan: For logging, do you keep PII in logs? Our policy forbids storing PHI outside customer control.
08:03 Samira: We support configurable redaction and can route audit logs to your Splunk. We'll also share our data deletion policies.
08:12 James: Legal will want an explicit data flow diagram.
08:15 Olivia: We'll include a diagram in the follow-up email.
08:20 (link paste noise)
08:35 Marcus: Next for the pilot plan — propose: Week 1: provisioning & smoke tests (connect VPC, KMS, initial model), Week 2: run workloads, collect metrics, evaluate quality and latency. Does that timeline match your availability?
08:52 Priya: Yes; our infra team can allocate a window in early April.
09:00 Maya: Who will be the point of contact for ops during provisioning?
09:04 Evan: That'll be me. I'll send contact and a calendar blocking for the peering window.
09:10 Marcus: Great. I'll follow up with a checklist of required network rules and an example Terraform snippet if you prefer IaC.
09:20 James: Terraform snippets would be great. Saves us time.
09:26 Olivia: Ok we'll attach those.
09:30 (short silence)
09:38 Priya: On contracts, any flexibility for month-by-month while we validate?
09:41 Olivia: For pilots we can do a short-term trial with usage-based billing; longer Dedicated commits are negotiated after pilot success.
09:50 James: And security review won't be a blocker for the pilot? We still need legal to sign an NDA and do a quick security questionnaire.
09:58 Samira: NDA is fine; we'll send the standard questionnaire. Security review for production gating can happen in parallel with the pilot.
10:06 (some typing)
10:18 Marcus: A couple of technical clarifications: what model family are you planning to use? Do you want us to recommend curated open models or a specific checkpoint?
10:28 James: We're open to Redwood's recommendations, but we want something that balances cost and hallucination risk — accuracy in clinical context is important.
10:38 Marcus: We'll recommend a model variant with safety fine-tuning and suggest hallucination mitigation patterns in prompts. We'll include eval metrics.
10:46 Olivia: Ok to recap next steps — Samira will send SOC2/security docs; Olivia will send onboarding checklist, runbook, and Terraform snippets; Marcus will prepare private deployment deep-dive and quantization recommendations; Evan to share VPC ranges and Splunk endpoint.
11:05 Priya: That works. Can we set a follow-up technical deep-dive meeting? Prefer week of 2026-03-23.
11:13 Marcus: Yes — Marcus and I are available Wed/Thu that week. We'll propose times.
11:20 James: Great. Anything else?
11:24 Maya: Just one more — monitoring: can we set alerts on regression of embedding recall?
11:29 Marcus: Yes, Redwood Optimize supports quality monitoring tied to eval prompt sets; you can set regression alerts. We'll show the console.
11:38 Olivia: Perfect. Thanks all — we'll send the follow-up email with attachments and proposed times for the deep-dive.
11:45 (overlap / thanks)
11:52 Priya: Thanks everyone. Looking forward.
11:55 Olivia: Thanks, bye.
12:00 Meeting end.

Notes about transcript: minor mis-transcriptions likely for some proper nouns; speaker attributions approximate; references shared: https://redwood/doc/onboarding-checklist (placeholder), SOC2 pack (shared by Samira), Terraform examples (shared by Marcus).
